title: Loose boards over a stairwell are not a cover — they are a missing temporary works item
excerpt: HSE press release 21 September 2026: Hillbeck Homes (Sowerby Bridge) Ltd was fined £300,000 plus £9,284.05 costs at Leeds Magistrates’ Court on 16 September 2026 after Joseph Tuck, 24, fell one storey through an unprotected stairwell opening on a four-dwelling site in January 2024. Loose scaffold boards that had previously covered the opening had been removed. There was no edge protection and no alternative sub-floor access. West Yorkshire Fire & Rescue and HART rescued him unconscious. He sustained serious spinal injuries and has not returned to a physical job. Floor openings are temporary works.
linkedinReady:
A stairwell waiting for a flight is not an empty hole. It is a temporary works opening with a one-storey drop onto concrete.

HSE published the outcome on 21 September 2026. Joseph Tuck, 24, a father of one and a temporary scaffolding labourer in his second week, stepped backwards through an unprotected stairwell on a four-house site being built by Hillbeck Homes (Sowerby Bridge) Ltd in January 2024. Loose scaffold boards that had sat over the opening had been removed. There was no edge protection. West Yorkshire Fire & Rescue and HART recovered him unconscious. He suffered serious spinal injuries and has not returned to a physical job.

The housebuilder was found guilty on three charges for failing to plan and supervise work at height and to prevent a fall. Fine: £300,000 plus £9,284.05 costs at Leeds Magistrates’ Court on 16 September 2026. HSE’s release does not allege an offence by the scaffolding employer.

Register the opening. Fit a secured cover or designed edge protection before anyone works next to it. Loose boards that can be lifted are not a cover.

Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

#TemporaryWorks #WorkAtHeight #HSE #EdgeProtection #BS5975

body.p: The Health and Safety Executive published a prosecution release on 21 September 2026. Joseph Tuck, 24, a father of one, was working as a temporary labourer for a scaffolding company in January 2024 on a site of four new domestic dwellings being constructed by Hillbeck Homes (Sowerby Bridge) Ltd. It was his second week on the job. He stepped backwards through an opening intended for a staircase that had not yet been installed and fell one storey onto a concrete floor. The stairwell opening had not been securely covered — previous loose scaffold boards had been removed — and the open edges were not protected. There were no alternative means of accessing the sub-floor. West Yorkshire Fire & Rescue and the HART team rescued Mr Tuck, who had fallen unconscious. He sustained serious spinal injuries, was unable to work for months, and has not returned to a physical job. Hillbeck Homes (Sowerby Bridge) Ltd, formerly of 1 Bretton Place, Otley Road, Guiseley, Leeds LS20 8FL, was found guilty on three charges: it failed to properly plan and appropriately supervise work at height and to take suitable and sufficient measures to prevent a fall. The company was fined £300,000 and ordered to pay £9,284.05 in costs at Leeds Magistrates’ Court on 16 September 2026. HSE Inspector Louise Redgrove said falls from height remain one of the leading causes of death in construction, accounting for around a quarter of all fatal injuries to workers each year, and that this was a wholly avoidable incident caused by basic failures in planning and supervision.

A stairwell, lift shaft, service riser or floor void before the permanent flight, slab or cover is in place is a temporary works item. The hazard is a fall through an opening, not only a fall from an external edge. Work at Height Regulations 2005 require suitable and sufficient measures to prevent a fall, including where there is a risk of falling through openings in floors, roofs or work platforms. CDM 2015 requires the principal contractor to plan, manage and monitor the construction phase. BS 5975-1:2024 is the management procedure that puts openings, edge protection, crash decks and scaffold interfaces on the temporary works register, names a Temporary Works Coordinator and Temporary Works Supervisor, and requires a design or standard solution, inspection and a permit before people work next to the void. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A domestic house plot can become high risk where boards are loose, covers are removed for access and not reinstated, there is no alternative route, and the person nearest the opening is new to site. The HSE release was brought against the housebuilder. Scaffold contractors still need their own interface control: do not leave a void because the housebuilder owns the hole.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register every stairwell, lift shaft, riser and floor opening as a temporary works item from first slab pour until the permanent flight or cover is fixed.
Specify a secured cover (fixed, marked, load-rated, not loose boards) or designed edge protection. Loose scaffold boards that can be lifted for access are not a cover.
If the cover must be removed for a task, treat removal as a controlled change: exclusion zone, alternative protection, named person, and reinstatement before the next trade walks the floor.
Plan access to the sub-floor. HSE recorded that there were no alternative means of accessing the sub-floor on this site — that is a planning failure, not a rescue problem.
Interface the scaffold contractor, housebuilder and follow-on trades on the same opening. The person who removes the boards is responsible for the void they leave.
Inspect openings at the start of each shift and after any board movement. Record the inspection. A missing cover is a stop.
Provisional design or check category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure. Public, multi-storey or occupied-building openings escalate.
Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a design, not a check and not a permit. Subject to project-specific verification of opening size, drop height, cover specification, edge protection, access routes, sequence and responsible persons, and to acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Facts, dates, fines, names and comments are taken from the HSE Media Centre release of 21 September 2026; confirm against that page before relying on them. Exact clause references in the Work at Height Regulations 2005, CDM 2015 and BS 5975-1:2024 are to be confirmed against the project licensed copy. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site. Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.
